what: Draws several scroll-bound scene images (like 120 rotating product frames) onto a single canvas. Once the panel progress passes 12%, the target frame is chosen 4x faster (so it all runs within 12~34% of the panel), and the current frame chases it by 8% of the remaining gap per frame, so it glides to a stop even after scrolling stops. If an image URL template is given, it preloads and draws 300px ahead of the screen. If not, it sends an fx:frame event (detail.frame, count) on the element so the consumer draws directly in 3D or canvas.
ease: none (progress → section number is a straight line) · each frame chases 8% of the remaining gap

options.src: Image URL pattern — section number goes here {i}(「frames/pack_{i}.webp”). If missing, only fires the fx:frame event
options.pad: Section number digit count (zero-padded), default 0 — original is 5 (00000)
options.start: Panel progress when it starts to turn (0–1), default .12
options.speed: Speed relative to progress, default 4 — reaches the last section in the (1−start)/4 range after start
options.lerp: Chase ratio per frame, default .08 — 1 jumps straight to that slide
options.trigger: CSS of the outer element that acts as the panel (default the element itself) — for when the long panel scrolls with the image fixed in place
options.[data-fx-part=canvas]: Canvas to draw on (if none, one is created inside the element, and if the element is a canvas, it is used)

use: — Without a picture: el.addEventListener("fx:frame", (e) => draw(e.detail.frame))
note: The original draws 120 webp frames on a canvas and runs rAF constantly. This part pauses rAF once it reaches the target frame and wakes it again when scrolling moves (drawing the same frame). With reduced motion it stays on the first frame

from.where: index.js fixed bag (.hs-pack__cv) — draws a three 3D bag in place of the original 120-frame rotating image (same flow as the fx:frame type)

index.js image sequence (original ImageSequence: from when the plate touches the bottom of the screen until it leaves upward, 120 frames played straight, preloaded by splitting in halves from the middle) — drawn directly with fx:frame, no images. To play it straight use start: 0; speed: 1; lerp: 1

detail.html .d-intro__spin — original ImageSequence 240 frames, with the canvas progress kept exactly as it exits from the screen bottom edge upward (start: 0; speed: 1; lerp: 1; frames: 240; enter: top bottom; leave: bottom top), the copy drives three devices via fx:frame

index.js scroll film — original ScrollFilm 222 frames (phone 218): from when the panel head touches the bottom of the screen, follows progress/.96 by 1−.78 per frame. The copy draws our own canvas scene per number, like fx:frame
from.options: frames: 222; start: 0; speed: 1.0417; lerp: .22; enter: top bottom; leave: bottom bottom
